questions.question: Until verified, how should dates, teacher details, submission route and component allocations be labelled?
questions.feedback: Unverified administrative details should remain clearly marked as needing teacher confirmation before being treated as facts.

questions.question: Which sequence best reflects the intended organisation of the report?
questions.feedback: The report should logically progress from the brief through production evidence to the final evaluation.

questions.question: According to the source boundary, what controls unresolved task details and evidence requirements?
options: The current Task 1 handbook, teacher-issued brief, drawings and submission directions
questions.feedback: When information is unresolved, authoritative task documents determine the correct requirements rather than assumptions.

sections.title: Final quality assurance and authentic submission

questions.question: What is the main purpose of final quality assurance?
options: Check both the finished project and its supporting evidence
questions.feedback: Final quality assurance verifies both the physical project and the folio accurately and consistently represent the completed work.

questions.question: What should the folio accurately represent?
questions.feedback: The folio should match the as-built result rather than an earlier plan or an idealised version.

questions.question: If an approved change was made during production, what should happen?
questions.feedback: Approved changes should be identified so the evidence accurately explains how the final result developed.

questions.question: Why should photographs, sketches and quality checks form a consistent account?
options: To support an accurate evidence chain
To reduce the number of folio pages
questions.feedback: Consistent evidence helps demonstrate that the folio truthfully documents the completed project from multiple sources.

questions.question: What should a student do if a fault remains unresolved?
questions.feedback: Honest reporting maintains the integrity of the submission even when problems remain unresolved.

questions.question: When may the folio state that a feature passed inspection?
options: Whenever the student believes it passed
After comparing it with similar projects
questions.feedback: Inspection claims must only be made after confirmation through the authorised process described by project requirements.

questions.question: Why should teacher-issued drawings, demonstrations and approved references be acknowledged?
options: To recognise sources that influenced decisions
questions.feedback: Acknowledging sources makes it clear where important decisions or information came from and supports authentic work.

questions.question: How should help with planning or production be presented?
options: Described as the student's own work
questions.feedback: Assistance should always be acknowledged rather than presented as original student work.

questions.question: Before submission, what should be checked about saved and printed evidence?
questions.feedback: Evidence should be complete, readable and correctly ordered so it can be followed and verified.

questions.question: According to the source boundary, what controls unresolved inspection and submission details?
options: The teacher-issued brief, drawings, criteria, handbook and submission directions
questions.feedback: When details remain unresolved, the authorised project documents determine the correct inspection and submission requirements.

sections.title: Reading the folding-shovel system through its drawings

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an assembly drawing?
questions.feedback: Assembly drawings explain how major parts relate, while detail drawings provide information about individual components.

questions.question: Why should students cross-reference assembly, detail and sectional views?
questions.feedback: Comparing multiple drawing views helps reveal relationships that cannot be understood from a single image alone.

questions.question: Which source should be used if a written dimension and the picture appear different?
questions.feedback: Written dimensions and notes are authoritative, while appearance should never override documented drawing information.

questions.question: What may a sectional view reveal that an outside view cannot?
questions.feedback: Sectional views expose hidden features and relationships that are not visible from external views alone.

questions.question: A feature shown on one component controls the fit of another. What does this demonstrate?
questions.feedback: A change to one component can influence another because the product operates as an interconnected system.

questions.question: Before marking or machining begins, what should students confirm?
options: Information controlling position, movement or fit
questions.feedback: Students should identify the information that governs position, movement and fit before practical work begins.

questions.question: Besides dimensions, what should be checked to ensure production uses the correct drawing?
questions.feedback: Checking component identity and revision helps ensure production follows the current approved drawing version.

questions.question: If drawing information is conflicting or unclear, what is the correct action?
options: Record the issue and refer it to the teacher
Scale the drawing to fill the gap
questions.feedback: Recording uncertainties and referring them creates an evidence trail and avoids unsupported assumptions.

questions.question: Why should students avoid scaling an image?

questions.question: Tracing each component across assembly, detail and sectional views before practical work mainly supports what?

sections.title: WMS planning for a multi-process product

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a whole-product Work Method Statement (WMS)?

questions.question: According to the theory, what should a WMS show between construction stages?
questions.feedback: Showing dependencies explains why one stage must be completed or checked before later work can continue safely and correctly.

questions.question: Why are quality hold points included in a whole-product WMS?

questions.question: How does the whole-product WMS differ from the metal-lathe SOP?

The WMS coordinates the overall project while the SOP covers the lathe process
questions.feedback: The WMS explains where lathe work fits into the project, while the SOP governs approved lathe operation.

questions.question: Which information is identified for each stage in the WMS?

questions.feedback: Each WMS stage records the task together with approved safety, permission and quality information needed for that step.

questions.question: A component has not passed its quality hold point. What should happen next?

Ignore the hold point if the part looks correct
questions.feedback: Hold points exist so later work does not rely on results that have not yet been confirmed.

The WMS replaces teacher supervision once completed
Teacher supervision is only needed for lathe work

questions.question: When an unresolved process detail is not stated in the WMS, what controls the correct action?

sections.title: Societal and environmental criteria before manufacture

questions.question: Why should societal and environmental impacts be considered before manufacture?

questions.question: Which question belongs in a balanced impact framework?

How durable and repairable is the product expected to be?

questions.question: What should societal criteria be based on?
options: The confirmed folding-camping-shovel context and reliable evidence
questions.feedback: Societal claims should reflect the confirmed project context and verified evidence rather than unsupported assumptions.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects environmental criteria?
options: Consider resources, waste, maintenance and end-of-life outcomes
questions.feedback: Environmental criteria examine the product's lifecycle, including resource use, waste, maintenance and end-of-life considerations.

questions.question: Why should students avoid describing the product as eco-friendly?
options: The term is only suitable after manufacture
The teacher must approve every environmental statement
Such claims require verified supporting information
questions.feedback: Broad environmental claims need reliable evidence before they can be presented as justified conclusions.

questions.question: Which example best shows an evidence-based trade-off?

Choosing the fastest option is always best
Reducing waste always improves service life

questions.question: If evidence about an impact is incomplete, what should the report do?

questions.question: Which claim follows the theory most closely?

Repairability is irrelevant once manufacture begins
Responsible long-term use should be considered using reliable evidence

questions.question: Which source should resolve uncertain impact details?

questions.question: Which pair of factors is specifically identified as a possible trade-off?

sections.title: Translating the shovel-head drawing into a controlled sequence

questions.question: Why should the drawing be read together with the teacher demonstration?

questions.question: What do orientation marks help preserve?

Before irreversible stages and before later work depends on the result

questions.question: Which documents should remain connected through traceability?

The classroom timetable and attendance roll
The equipment catalogue and supplier brochure

sections.title: Material behaviour during forming and shaping

questions.question: According to the theory, hardness mainly affects a material's resistance to what?

questions.question: What may influence how strongly a workpiece resists a change in shape?
questions.feedback: Thickness can influence resistance during forming, so observations should be linked to verified material information.

questions.question: If a confirmed material has a manufacturing direction, what may affect how consistently it forms?

questions.question: What is work hardening?
options: A material becoming more resistant to further shaping after repeated deformation
A material permanently returning to its original shape
A material becoming softer after repeated deformation
questions.feedback: Work hardening occurs after repeated deformation, increasing resistance to further shaping rather than reducing it.

questions.question: What is springback?
options: A surface becoming harder after cutting
A material partly returning towards its earlier form after shaping force is removed
questions.feedback: Springback is partial recovery towards the earlier shape after the forming force is removed.

questions.question: A material behaves differently from expected during approved work. What should students do first?

questions.question: Which combination should students observe during approved work?

questions.question: Why should students avoid assuming the cause of an unexpected material response?

Because an unexpected response does not prove a cause by itself
Because drawings always explain unexpected behaviour

questions.question: According to the source boundary, what controls unresolved forming, shaping and material-behaviour details?

questions.question: What should be recorded before suggesting a possible cause of a problem?

questions.question: Which evidence best supports an inspection record?

questions.question: If inspection results are uncertain, what should happen before assembly continues?

questions.question: Which detail should inspection evidence identify?

questions.question: Why should a shovel head not proceed simply because later components are ready?
options: Assembly readiness depends only on appearance

questions.question: According to the source boundary, what controls unresolved inspection, acceptance and correction details?

sections.title: Metal-lathe SOP evidence for handle and end-plug work

questions.question: According to the theory, what should strong SOP evidence identify?

questions.question: Where must exact machining actions come from?

A comparison with the verified drawing and approved criteria
An estimate based on appearance alone

questions.question: If equipment differs from the demonstrated setup, what should students do first?

sections.title: Functional fits connect dimensions to movement and assembly

questions.question: What does a functional fit describe?
options: The surface appearance of a component
The dimensional relationship between components that assemble or operate together
The machining sequence for producing a component
questions.feedback: A functional fit explains how related components dimensionally interact during assembly or operation, not how they look or were made.

questions.question: Which fit category always requires parts to engage tightly?
questions.feedback: An interference fit requires tight engagement, unlike clearance or transition fits, which may allow some space or slight variation.

questions.question: Why should students connect verified dimensions to functional purpose?
options: To understand how dimensions influence movement, alignment and assembly
To improve the appearance of machined surfaces
questions.feedback: Dimensions should be interpreted through their functional role so machining supports correct assembly, movement and long-term performance.

questions.question: What should determine the required fit for the shovel project?
options: The teacher-issued drawing and acceptance criteria
questions.feedback: General fit categories describe possibilities, but the required project fit comes from verified drawings and acceptance criteria.

questions.question: According to the theory, what is the purpose of progressive inspection?
options: To confirm the component remains suitable before more material is removed or assembly begins
To replace the need for final inspection
To improve the visual finish after machining
questions.feedback: Progressive inspection helps identify developing issues early, reducing the risk of removing unnecessary material before assembly.

questions.question: Why is appearance alone insufficient for confirming a functional fit?
options: Because functional relationships must be checked against verified drawings and teacher-controlled criteria
Because polished surfaces always hide defects
questions.feedback: A component may appear correct yet still fail functional requirements, so verified drawing information and criteria must be used.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a transition fit?

questions.question: Besides assembly and movement, what else can a suitable fit influence?

The colour of the finished component

Ignore the problem if the parts still fit together

questions.question: According to the key takeaways, dimensional checks should primarily be linked to what?

sections.title: Threads as controlled geometry and evidence

The lowest area between adjacent crests

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a teacher-approved thread gauge or checking method?

To make any thread fit during assembly
To estimate the thread size by feel

questions.question: If a thread shows resistance during engagement, what should a student do?

Replace it with a similar-looking fastener

questions.question: What does the major diameter of a thread describe?

questions.question: Why should a generic fastener not automatically replace a specified thread?

Generic fasteners cannot have external threads

questions.question: Which information should be recorded during thread inspection?

Only whether the thread looked acceptable
Only the component name and date

The thread is formed within an opening
The thread has the largest major diameter

sections.title: Pivot parts: centres, alignment and movement path

From the approved drawing and teacher criteria

The external shape of the assembled parts

The appearance of the finished surface

sections.title: Societal and environmental impact report with evidence

questions.question: What should be the main basis for judging the completed shovel's impacts?
options: Evidence from the completed project and credible referenced sources
What usually happens in metalwork projects
questions.feedback: Impact judgements should come from verified project evidence and acknowledged credible sources, not assumptions or generalisations.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the relationship between societal and environmental impacts?
options: Evidence for one category automatically proves the other
The categories are connected but each requires its own supporting evidence
questions.feedback: Societal and environmental impacts may relate, but each conclusion still needs appropriate supporting evidence.

questions.question: A student claims the shovel is sustainable without providing supporting evidence. What should the report do instead?
options: State the product is sustainable because it was completed
Explain benefits, limitations and supporting evidence
questions.feedback: Balanced reports explain strengths, limitations and supporting evidence rather than making unsupported sustainability claims.

questions.question: Which source provides the strongest evidence for resource use in the project?
options: A guess based on the finished product
questions.feedback: Recorded project evidence is stronger than opinions or assumptions when judging resource use.

questions.question: Why should an impact report discuss trade-offs?
options: Because every production decision has only positive effects
Because improvements in one area may increase impacts in another
Because trade-offs are only required for environmental impacts
questions.feedback: Production decisions can improve function or serviceability while increasing material use, processing or waste.

questions.question: If information needed to support an impact claim is unavailable, what should the report do?
options: State the limitation instead of inventing a conclusion
questions.feedback: Evidence-first reporting recognises limitations instead of filling gaps with unsupported conclusions.

questions.question: Which combination represents stronger evidence than assumptions?
options: Production photographs, waste observations and documented quality checks
A description based only on appearance
questions.feedback: Recorded project evidence provides stronger support than opinions or observations without documentation.

questions.question: Where should unresolved impact claims be checked before being included in the report?
options: Teacher-issued requirements, project records and approved referenced sources
A social media post about metal products
questions.feedback: Teacher-issued sources, verified project records and approved references control unresolved impact claims.

questions.question: A report argues that durability reduces early replacement. According to the theory, what else is needed?
options: Evidence about construction quality and intended use
A statement that all metal products last longer
No further evidence because durability proves the claim
questions.feedback: Claims about reduced replacement require supporting evidence linking durability with construction quality and intended use.

questions.question: Why should external information be acknowledged correctly in the report?
options: To make the report appear longer
Because credible external facts must be properly referenced
Because project evidence cannot be used
questions.feedback: Credible external information strengthens the report only when it is properly acknowledged alongside project evidence.

sections.title: PMI, project report and authentic Task 2 submission

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the final PMI evaluation and project report?
options: To consolidate the complete evidence chain for the project
questions.feedback: The report brings together verified planning, production and evaluation evidence rather than adding unrelated new material.

questions.question: Which combination of evidence best reflects the report described in this section?
options: Only the finished photographs and final product
Planning, production, costing, quality and impact evidence
A personal opinion about the project
questions.feedback: The report should connect planning, production, costing, quality checks, impacts and evaluation into one supported evidence chain.

questions.question: A photograph in the folio is most useful when it includes a caption that:
options: Explains the production stage, what the image proves and its connection to a decision or criterion
States that the work looks good
questions.feedback: Strong captions explain the evidence shown and link it directly to project decisions or assessment criteria.

questions.question: How should cost evidence and component records be presented?
options: Adjusted to match the original plan
Recorded to reflect what was actually used and made
questions.feedback: Authentic records should accurately reflect the completed project rather than estimates or planned values.

questions.question: Which PMI point best follows the guidance in this section?
options: The handle worked well because I liked it
The assembly was successful because it looked professional
The folding action was smooth, improving usability, likely due to accurate alignment shown in recorded checks
questions.feedback: Each PMI point should describe an effect and, where supported by evidence, identify a likely cause.

questions.question: What should you do if faults or missing evidence remain before submission?
options: Hide them so the report appears complete
Record them honestly as part of the as-built project
Remove any photographs showing the problem
questions.feedback: Authentic submission requires honest reporting of faults, missing evidence and unresolved issues rather than concealing them.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects authentic submission?
options: Only successful work should be included
Changes, assistance and unresolved approval should be acknowledged
Every planned feature must be reported as completed
questions.feedback: Authentic submissions accurately acknowledge assistance, changes and unresolved approval instead of presenting an idealised project.

questions.question: Where should you confirm unresolved assessment details such as submission directions or approval status?
options: The current Task 2 handbook, teacher-issued documents and teacher directions
questions.feedback: Teacher-issued sources control unresolved assessment details and should always be checked before making assumptions.

questions.question: Why should the project report link the brief, drawings, WMS, SOP evidence and production records?
options: To show how evidence connects across the completed project
questions.feedback: Connecting related evidence demonstrates how planning, production and evaluation support the completed project as a whole.

questions.question: A report includes the teacher's name, issue date and approval status without checking official sources. According to this section, what should the student do?
options: Refer to teacher-issued sources because those details remain teacher to confirm until formally verified
questions.feedback: Where assessment details remain unresolved, students should rely on teacher-issued sources rather than assumptions or estimates.
